sub: Named after “the ways of ascent” in ayah 3
theme: A warning to those who mocked the Day of Judgement and dared the Prophet ﷺ to bring the punishment on. The whole surah answers that denial.
story: Revealed in Makkah, in the same setting as Al-Ḥāqqah. The Prophet ﷺ warned the disbelievers about the resurrection, Paradise and Hell, and they turned it into a joke.

They gathered around him in groups, mocked the believers, and joked that they would enter Paradise first. One of them, reportedly an-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, even dared Allah: “If this is the truth, rain stones down on us” (8:32).

The surah is Allah’s reply. The punishment is certain, that Day is terrifying, only the people of prayer are saved, and the mockers will meet their Day. Throughout, the Prophet ﷺ is told to be patient.

sections.title: The punishment they asked for is coming
sections.meaning: Someone demanded the punishment, mocking it. It will fall on the disbelievers, it comes from Allah, and nothing can hold it back. So the Prophet ﷺ is told to be patient: they think it is far off, Allah sees it near.
points: A questioner asks for the punishment; no one can stop it
From Allah, Lord of the ways of ascent; a Day of 50,000 years
They see it far; We see it near
sections.matters: It opens with the challenge and answers it at once: the punishment is real, it comes from Allah, and no one can stop it. It also gives the Prophet ﷺ the surah’s key instruction, to be patient beautifully.
sections.story: A disbeliever, reportedly an-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, mocked the warnings and prayed: “O Allah, if this is the truth, rain stones on us or bring us a painful punishment.” He was later killed at Badr.
explained: Saʾala sāʾil here means someone demanded the punishment, not just asked about it. The reply: it will fall on the disbelievers, and it comes from dhī al-maʿārij, the Lord of the ways of ascent, the heavens the angels rise through.

The angels and Jibrīl rise to Him. The Day of fifty thousand years is crushing for the disbeliever and lighter than one prayer for the believer. So be patient: they think that Day is far off, even impossible, but Allah sees it near.
teaches: Never mock or challenge Allah’s warning.
What is coming is near, so live like it.
The long Day is light for those who prepared.
sections.hook: The surah’s name comes from ayah 3 (dhī al-maʿārij). Ayah 4 shows who climbs: the angels and the Rūḥ.

sections.title: The terrors of that Day
sections.meaning: The sky like murky oil, mountains like wool. No friend asks about a friend. The criminal would hand over his children, wife, brother, clan and everyone on earth to be saved. No! The Fire calls the one who turned away and hoarded.
points: Sky like murky oil, mountains like wool
No friend asks a friend; the criminal would ransom everyone
No! It is the Flame, stripping away the skin
It calls whoever turned away and hoarded wealth
sections.matters: Section 1 said the Day is near. This section shows what it looks like, and destroys the idea that family, tribe or wealth can save anyone.
sections.story: No specific incident. It continues the reply to those who laughed at the Day.
explained: The sky melts like dregs of oil and the mountains float like fluffed wool. Close friends see each other, but no one asks about anyone else. Everyone is consumed with himself.

The criminal would hand over his children, wife, brother, whole clan, even everyone on earth, just to escape. Never. It is Laẓā, a blazing Fire that strips off the skin. It calls by name those who turned from the truth and those who hoarded wealth without paying what was due on it.
teaches: No one can carry you on that Day, not even family.
Turning away means both denying in the heart and neglecting in action.
sections.hook: The ransom list grows outward: children → wife → brother → clan → the whole earth. It ends with hoarding (18), and the next section answers with “a known right” in wealth (24).

sections.title: Man is impatient, except those who pray
sections.meaning: Man is anxious by nature: he panics when hardship hits and holds back when good comes. The exception is the people of prayer, and a list of their qualities follows. They will be honoured in gardens.
points: Anxious: panics in hardship, withholds in ease
A known share of wealth for the asker and the deprived
Believe in the Day of Recompense, fear their Lord
Guard their prayer → honoured in gardens
sections.matters: The turning point of the surah. After the terror comes the way out: human nature is weak, and prayer, together with the character it builds, is the cure.
sections.story: No specific incident. It describes the two kinds of people, those headed for Paradise and those headed for the Fire. The same list of qualities opens Sūrat al-Muʾminūn.
explained: Man is halūʿ: anxious and greedy. He panics when hardship hits and holds back when good comes. He is judged not for this tendency but for what he chooses to do with it.

The exception is the people of prayer. They pray consistently, give a fixed share to those in need, believe in the Day of Judgement, fear their Lord, stay chaste, keep trusts and promises, testify honestly, and guard their prayer. The list starts and ends with prayer. Their reward is honour in gardens.
teaches: Prayer is the cure for both panic and stinginess.
Small but consistent beats big but occasional.
Give from your wealth, including to the needy who don’t ask.
Keep your word, your trusts and your testimony.
sections.hook: Prayer bookends the list, at ayah 23 (dāʾimūn) and ayah 34 (yuḥāfiẓūn). The section starts at the ۞ mark on page 569.

sections.title: Warning to the mockers
sections.meaning: The disbelievers hurry around the Prophet ﷺ in groups, right and left, and still expect Paradise. No! Allah can replace them with people better than them. So leave them to their games until their promised Day, when they rush from the graves, eyes lowered in disgrace.
points: Hurrying around you, right and left, in groups
Each hopes for Paradise? No! We made them from what they know
By the Lord of the risings and settings: We can replace them
Leave them until the promised Day: rushing out, eyes humbled
sections.matters: The surah comes full circle: it opened with a demand for punishment and closes with “the Day they were promised.” It exposes the mockers’ false hope and comforts the Prophet ﷺ.
sections.story: Disbelievers would crowd around the Prophet ﷺ in circles, stare at him, mock him and his companions, and say: “If these people enter Paradise, we will enter it before them.” These ayat were revealed about them.
explained: Why do they rush around you, splitting into groups, and still expect Paradise? Never. They were made from a drop of fluid, like everyone else. Paradise comes through faith and obedience, not wishful thinking, and the One who made them from a drop can easily bring them back.

Allah swears by the Lord of every sunrise and sunset that He can replace them with better people, and nothing escapes Him. So leave them to their games. On their Day they will rush out of the graves toward the caller, eyes lowered, covered in humiliation.
teaches: Hope without faith and deeds is empty.
Your own creation proves the resurrection.
sections.hook: There are two rushes: toward the Prophet ﷺ to mock (36) and out of the graves (43). The surah opens with “a punishment bound to happen” and closes with “the Day they were promised.”

groups.text: Someone demanded the punishment. It will hit the disbelievers, no one can stop it, and it comes from Allah, Lord of the heavens.
The angels and Jibrīl rise to Him. The Day of 50,000 years is long for the disbeliever and lighter than one prayer for the believer.
Be patient, without complaining. They think the Day is far away; Allah sees it near.
The sky melts like dregs of oil, and the mountains become like fluffed wool.
Friends see each other but don’t ask about each other. The criminal would give up his family, clan and the whole earth to escape.
Never! It is Laẓā, a blazing Fire that strips off the skin.
The Fire calls those who turned from the truth and hoarded wealth.
Man is anxious by nature: he panics in hardship and holds back in ease.
Except those who pray, and pray consistently.
They give a fixed share of their wealth to those who ask and those in need.
They believe in the Day of Judgement and fear their Lord’s punishment.
They stay chaste, within what Allah made lawful.
They keep their trusts and promises and testify honestly.
They guard their prayer, and they are honoured in gardens.
The disbelievers crowd around the Prophet ﷺ in scattered groups, mocking.
They hope for Paradise? Never. They were made from a drop, like everyone else.
By the Lord of every sunrise and sunset, Allah can replace them with better.
Leave them until their Day: rushing from the graves, eyes lowered in shame.

1.explain: Saʾala sāʾil: someone demanded the punishment, mocking and challenging. Wāqiʿ: it will definitely happen.
1.why: Reportedly an-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who prayed: “If this is the truth, rain stones on us” (8:32). He was killed at Badr. Another report says Makkah’s disbelievers asked who the punishment was meant for.

2.explain: It is for the disbelievers, earned by their stubborn denial. No one can stop it before it comes or lift it once it lands.

3.explain: It comes from Allah, dhī al-maʿārij: Lord of the heavens the angels rise through, Lord of the highest ranks. If they knew His greatness, they would never dare rush His punishment.

4.explain: The angels and Jibrīl rise to Him. The 50,000 years is either the Day of Judgement (long for disbelievers, lighter than one prayer for believers) or the distance the angels cover in a single day.

5.explain: Ṣabr jamīl: patience without panic or complaint. Keep calling people to Allah even when they don’t listen. This came before fighting was permitted.

6.explain: They see the Day as far away, really as something that will never happen.

7.explain: Allah sees it as near and certain. He doesn’t rush it, but whatever is coming is close.

8.explain: The sky becomes like al-muhl: dregs of oil, or molten metal. It splits apart from the terror of that Day.

9.explain: The mountains become like al-ʿihn: dyed, fluffed wool blown about by the wind. If mountains are shaken like this, imagine a weak person heavy with sins.

10.explain: No ḥamīm, no close friend, asks about his friend. Each is too consumed with himself.

11.explain: They see and recognise each other, yet don’t speak. The criminal wishes he could ransom himself with his own children.

12.explain: …and his wife and his brother. He would give up even the child dearest to him.

13.explain: …and his faṣīlah, the clan that always protected him. On that Day no one can help anyone.

14.explain: …and everyone on earth, if it would save him. It wouldn’t: no ransom is accepted, not even a world full of gold.

15.explain: Kallā: never! There is no escape. Laẓā is a name of Hell, meaning the blazing flame.

16.explain: It strips away ash-shawā: the skin of the head, the limbs, flesh from bone.

17.explain: The Fire calls by name those who turned their backs on faith, “To me, to me!”, and picks them out the way a bird picks up seeds.

18.explain: …and those who gathered wealth and locked it away without paying Allah’s due on it.

19.explain: Halūʿ: intensely greedy and impatient. This is raw human nature, and the next two ayat define it.

20.explain: When hardship hits (poverty, illness, losing someone) he panics, with no patience and no acceptance of what Allah decreed.

21.explain: When good comes, he holds on to it and neither spends nor gives thanks. Allah tests us by asking us to give what we love and endure what we dislike.

22.explain: Except the people of prayer. They thank Allah and give in good times, and stay patient in hard times.

23.explain: Dāʾimūn: consistent in prayer, praying on time, properly and with focus, not turning left and right. Not like those who pray on and off or carelessly.

24.explain: A ḥaqq maʿlūm, a known and fixed right in their wealth: zakah and charity.

25.explain: It is for the sāʾil, who asks, and the maḥrūm, the poor person too dignified to ask, whom no one notices.

26.explain: They are certain of the Day of Judgement, so they prepare for it and work for the Hereafter.

27.explain: They fear their Lord’s punishment, so they avoid whatever leads to it.

28.explain: No one can feel safe from Allah’s punishment, except through His protection.

29.explain: They guard their chastity: no unlawful acts, and they avoid the looks and paths that lead there.

30.explain: With their spouses, and those their right hands possess, there is no blame.

31.explain: Anyone who goes beyond that crosses from what is lawful into what is forbidden.

32.explain: They take care of every trust and promise: duties to Allah that only He sees, and what people trust them with, such as money, secrets and agreements.

33.explain: They testify only to what they know: adding nothing, hiding nothing, and favouring no one, not even family.

34.explain: They guard their prayer: on time and done completely. Ayah 23 was about focus in prayer; this one is about keeping its times.

35.explain: They are honoured in gardens forever, with everything the soul desires.

36.explain: Muhṭiʿīn: rushing at the Prophet ﷺ, necks stretched out and staring, but only to find fault and mock.
36.why: Revealed about disbelievers who sat around the Prophet ﷺ, listening only so they could mock and deny him.

37.explain: ʿIzīn: in separate circles on his right and left, each group pleased with itself and mocking the believers.

38.explain: Does each of them really expect to enter Paradise while denying the Prophet ﷺ? On what basis?
38.why: They used to say: “If these people enter Paradise, we will enter it before them, and get more than them.” This ayah answered them.

39.explain: Kallā: never. They were made from a drop of fluid, like everyone else. Paradise comes through faith and taqwā, not status.

40.explain: Allah swears by the Lord of the easts and wests, the different points where the sun, moon and stars rise and set each day. They are signs of His power to resurrect.

41.explain: He can replace them with better, more obedient people, or bring them back exactly as they were. Nothing escapes Him.

42.explain: Leave them to their empty talk and games until their promised Day, when they will face the result.

43.explain: They rush out of the graves to answer the call, as if racing to a raised flag (or, in one reading, to the idols they used to race to touch).

44.explain: Eyes lowered and covered in humiliation, in return for their arrogance. That is the Day they were promised, and Allah’s promise always comes true.
